overview: This bill, the FREEDOM Act, requires the State Department, working with the Federal Communications Commission and the Treasury Department, to give Congress an updated report within 120 days on efforts to expand internet freedom in Iran, where the government censors and shuts down internet access. The report must assess whether technology that connects phones directly to satellites could get Iranians online, how jamming and drones could interfere, and who owns Iran's telecommunications companies. It must also review how well low-Earth-orbit satellite internet worked during Iran's January 2026 protests, its cost per user, and security risks for users, and whether ordinary off-the-shelf products could qualify for an existing federal grant program for internet access tools. As of February 10, 2026, the Senate Foreign Relations Committee had approved it and it was awaiting a vote by the full Senate.
for: Supporters say a detailed, up-to-date study will help the United States find practical ways to keep Iranians connected to the outside world when their government cuts off the internet.
against: Critics say the bill only orders another report rather than taking action, and that publicizing efforts to get around Iran's controls could raise safety risks for users inside the country.
